overall: The AG found the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to periodically review executive session minutes, but found no violation in the noticed executive session topic that omitted the employee's name.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board failed to identify the subject of its May 15, 2018 executive session, which was noticed as strategy for nonunion personnel negotiations without naming the employee.
allegations.key_passage: Given the sensitive nature of negotiating an employee’s separation, we find that the Board was justified in noticing the executive session topic without identifying the employee by name.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board failed to conduct a periodic review of its executive session minutes; the last review was in 2016.
allegations.key_passage: Here, because the Board had not conducted a periodic review of its executive session minutes in approximately two years, since 2016, it violated the Open Meeting Law in this regard.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law's requirements
remedy_passage: We order immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law’s requirements, and we caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
